newsitem.title: HUNGARY: OPEL TO BUILD 460,000 ENGINES/YR IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: OPEL TO BUILD 460,000 ENGINES/YR IN HUNGARY.

text.p: Opel Hungary Ltd said it will build 460,000 engines and 460,000 engine cylinder heads a year at capacity at the new 285 million German marks facilities officially opened on Friday.

Opel Hungary started engine production in 1992 with limited value added domesticly. The introduction of cylinder head production at the new facilities will increase the Hungarian contribution to the completed engines, company officials said.

"Our original investment...is nearly tripled by the new investment to over 700 million German marks - the largest automotive investment in Hungary," said Richard Donnelly, President of General Motors Europe AG at the opening of the new facilities in Western Hungary.
Opel Hungary is wholly owned by German automaker Adam Opel AG, a subsidiary of U.S. automaker General Motors Corp.
Opel hungary sad earlier it plans to build 299,000 engines in 1996. The company built 266,051 engines in 1995.
